habitat: Pairs and small flocks over large-tree woodland, mostly near water. The mud nest is in a cavity of a large tree, often near baobabs.
summary: A fairly common, localised resident. Metallic blue above, with a white throat and upper breast and deep orange on the rest of the underbody. In flight the underwing coverts are white and the tail-shafts are shorter than a Red-breasted Swallow’s. The call is a nasal harrrp, occasionally a guttural chuckle. It flutters, then glides, often high, and skims dams. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Red-breasted Swallow is orange-chestnut below, including the throat, with buff underwing coverts and a cap that reaches below the eyes.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^9=512 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 256–1024.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

underparts.pattern: White throat and upper breast. The rest of the underbody is deep orange.

White underwing coverts. Fluttering bursts are followed by a glide.
White upper breast, then deep orange, with white underwing coverts.

calls.description: A nasal, tin-trumpet-like harrrp, occasionally a guttural chuckle. No grade A recording was in the set. Grade B call from Awelani Lodge, Limpopo. The filename names Mosque Swallows. A Pafuri file is the same grade.
